instruction: Convert the Excel spreadsheet to HTML, save it to Desktop, and open it in a new Chrome tab.

metadata.explanation: Task requires HTML conversion and Chrome tab opening. Evaluator checks file creation (50%) and Chrome viewing (50%).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for HTML file created, 0.5 for HTML opened in Chrome tab

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - metric accesses expected.get('html_url_pattern') and expected.get('html_path') directly without attempting expected.get('rules')
Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies all instruction requirements - HTML file creation (50%) and Chrome tab opening (50%)
Postconfig appropriately handles UI state - opens HTML file in Chrome to ensure tab is available for verification
Data flow is correct: getter extracts file existence and Chrome tabs, metric compares both aspects with 50/50 weighting
Getter includes basic HTML validation - checks for HTML markers (<html, <!doctype html, <table) and minimum 100 byte size, not just file existence
Chrome tab verification uses exact URL pattern matching - checks if html_url_pattern is in tab URL
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: HTML validation is minimal - only checks for presence of HTML markers (<html, <table, <!doctype) and >100 bytes. Doesn't verify the file contains actual converted Excel data or that conversion was successful. A corrupted or empty HTML file with basic tags could pass.
No verification that source Excel file was actually used for conversion - any HTML file at the target path would pass, regardless of whether it came from the Excel spreadsheet
Getter hardcodes file path (/home/user/Desktop/annual-enterprise-survey-2021-financial-year-provisional.html) instead of reading from expected dict, reducing flexibility
